title: Prohibition on remuneration for referrals or business generation
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 9.01(11) a licensee may not offer, solicit or receive remuneration or anything of value to or from any person who owns, operates, manages or is an employee of a hospital, nursing home or other health care facility in return for a referral to a pharmacy, pharmacist, pharmacy technician or pharmacy intern, or for the generation of business from the sale or furnishing of any drugs, devices or services to any such persons or institutions.
exam_relevance: Tests that the prohibition runs in both directions and covers anything of value, not only cash payments.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

common_confusions: The bar covers offering as well as receiving, and anything of value rather than money alone.
Generating business is covered even without an individual patient referral.
verification_notes: Read verbatim in the current official Board of Registration in Pharmacy publication of 247 CMR 9.00 on 2026-08-19 during Batch 3 tranche B3-B authoring under Issue #91. A fresh independent legal and full-bank realism audit is still required before release.
